newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX booms ahead, spurred by Wall St, dollar.
newsitem.headline: German DAX booms ahead, spurred by Wall St, dollar.

text.p: A powerful overnight performance on Wall Street and bullish dollar powered German shares to fresh heights on Thursday morning, as the market continued its biggest ever bull run.
"We are off like a rocket again," said a Frankfurt dealer. "There has to come a time when people ask themselves why how long this frantic action can go on, but it doesn't look like today's the day."

The blue chip DAX index hit a record 4,245.88 points in early trade and was up 40.34 points, or one percent at 4.241.58 at 0844 GMT. In pre-bourse trade, the IBIS DAX hit a new alltime high of 4,272.55 points.
September DTB DAX futures, having briefly popped over the psychologically key 4,300 point level, were up 38.50 points at 4,262.19.

The main early spur for the market was the surge on Wall Street which took the Dow Jones Index above 8,000 points for the first time. The dollar's firm stance at just below 1.80 marks was another key support.
Retailer Karstadt AG was the top performer of the day, building on its six percent advance on Wednesday to trade up more than six percent at 705 marks.

Diverse speculation was circulating in the market about the company, including talk that it was a takeover target. Analysts are also upbeat about a pilot project running in one of its outlets designed to boost profits.
Some dealers were dubious about the outlook for more rapid gains on the broad market.

A virtually uninterrupted rally has lifted the DAX 11 percent this month alone and the blue chip index has gained 45 percent this year -- an almost inconceivable performance given that some early forecasts for the year had set targets for the DAX of around 3,300 points.
"Everyone is talking about a correction. The problem is that nobody is selling," said a dealer.

At the same time, dealers noted today's gains were partly driven by covering operations ahead of an expiry deadline for DAX contracts on the DTB futures and options exchange tomorrow. That upped the chance of a correction kicking in on Friday.
